1 │ # A lock file that lists no allowed environments is not taken seriously
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ A lock file can name the environments it is meant for. That list sits in a
   6 │ place called environments. Today, when that list is empty, the program skips
   7 │ the check that compares the list with my environment. It treats an empty list
   8 │ the same way it treats a lock file that says nothing about environments at all.
   9 │ So a lock file that on purpose says "no environment is allowed" behaves as if
  10 │ it allows every environment, and I get packages back with no warning.
  11 │ 
  12 │ ## What should happen
  13 │ 
  14 │ When a lock file lists environments but the list is empty, no environment can
  15 │ match it. I should get the clear error message that says my environment does
  16 │ not satisfy any of the environments named in the lock file. When a lock file
  17 │ says nothing about environments, then nothing should be restricted and I should
  18 │ get my packages as before.
  19 │ 
  20 │ ## About this project
  21 │ 
  22 │ This project is a set of tools for reading information about Python packages.
  23 │ One of the things it reads is a lock file, which records exactly which
  24 │ packages and versions belong to a project. People use these files to get the
  25 │ same packages every time, on the machines they choose.
  26 │ 
  27 │ ## Problem this solves
  28 │ 
  29 │ When a lock file deliberately allows no environments, I cannot trust it,
  30 │ because the file is quietly ignored and I still get packages. I need the tools
  31 │ to respect what the file says, so that a lock file with no allowed
  32 │ environments fails loudly instead of silently handing me a result.
  33 │ 
  34 │ ## What changed
  35 │ 
  36 │ An empty list of allowed environments in a lock file is now treated as a real
  37 │ restriction, not as if the list were absent. The old behavior, where an empty
  38 │ list simply let every environment through, is gone. A lock file that does not
  39 │ mention environments at all keeps working the same way as before, with no
  40 │ restriction.
  41 │ 
  42 │ ## Impact
  43 │ 
  44 │ Correctness and trust in lock files.
  45 │ 
  46 │ ## User experience
  47 │ 
  48 │ Before: I point the tool at a lock file whose list of allowed environments is
  49 │ empty, and it returns packages for my machine as if the list did not matter.
  50 │ After: I point the tool at that same lock file and get the error that my
  51 │ environment does not satisfy any of the environments named in the lock file.
  52 │ A lock file with no list at all still returns my packages.
  53 │
